symbols.name: n
symbols.role: Number of observed vertices.

symbols.name: V
symbols.role: Observed variables.

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: \(I_T\) denotes the nonstochastic regime indicator for intervention on \(T\).
symbols.role: Rule-2 action--observation exchanges.

symbols.name: COPAG0
symbols.def: The input-free COPAG class of Chen--Mooij.
symbols.role: Graphical model class.

symbols.name: PAG
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P=(\varnothing,V,E)\).
symbols.role: Observed equivalence-class graph.

symbols.name: Buckets
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak B(\mathcal P)=(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\) is a fixed deterministic ordering of the buckets of \(\mathcal P\).
symbols.role: Defines the admissible role intersections.

symbols.name: X
symbols.role: Original intervention coordinates.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.role: Outcome coordinates.

symbols.name: C
symbols.role: Original conditioning coordinates.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=X\cup C\).
symbols.role: Coordinates allowed to exchange intervention and observation roles.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: The selected cohort is the event \(S=\mathbf 1\).
symbols.role: Latent-selection event.

symbols.name: Ub
symbols.def: \(U_b\) is the latent common-cause vertex in the selected-bow template.
symbols.role: Bow-local latent vertex.

symbols.name: Xb
symbols.def: \(X_b\) is the treatment vertex in the selected-bow template.
symbols.role: Bow-local treatment vertex.

symbols.name: Yb
symbols.def: \(Y_b\) is the outcome vertex in the selected-bow template.
symbols.role: Bow-local outcome vertex.

symbols.name: Cb
symbols.def: \(C_b\) is the isolated conditioning vertex in the selected-bow template.
symbols.role: Bow-local conditioning vertex.

symbols.name: Sb
symbols.def: \(S_b\) is the selection vertex in the selected-bow template.
symbols.role: Bow-local selection vertex.

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.role: Indexes the two rational selected-bow mechanisms.

symbols.name: r
symbols.role: Centers the outcome mechanisms in the selected-bow template.

symbols.name: Mdplus
symbols.def: The positive discrete selected-SCM class represented by \(\mathcal P\) in Chen--Mooij.
symbols.role: Published identification domain before the binary-observed restriction.

symbols.name: M
symbols.role: Generic member used to define the published positive discrete model class.

symbols.name: Mplus
symbols.role: Identification domain.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M}=P_{\mathbf M}(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\).
symbols.role: Available population information.

symbols.name: psi
symbols.def: \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid \operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)\).
symbols.role: Target estimand.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) with \(\bar X\dot\cup\bar C=W\).
symbols.role: A treatment--condition allocation.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) is rooted at \((X,C)\) and contains exactly the states reachable through legal bucket-intersection Rule-2 exchanges.
symbols.role: Exhaustive conditional search space.

symbols.name: sIDP
symbols.def: Chen--Mooij's sound and complete algorithm for unconditional selected interventional kernels on input-free COPAGs.
symbols.role: Terminal joint-identification oracle.

symbols.name: CIDP
symbols.def: Jaber--Ribeiro--Zhang--Bareinboim's complete conditional-PAG algorithm without selection.
symbols.role: No-selection benchmark.

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: \(J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y,\bar C=\bar c\mid \operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1)\).
symbols.role: Joint target submitted to sIDP.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)=\sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}^Y}J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\).
symbols.role: Quantity locked by a failure certificate.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)\).
symbols.role: Quantity separated by a failure certificate.

symbols.name: Frho
symbols.def: \(F_{\rho}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is the formula returned by sIDP for \(J_{\rho}\), when that call succeeds.
symbols.role: Numerator functional on a successful branch.

symbols.name: Branch
symbols.role: Graph-and-query procedure returning a symbolic observed-law formula or \(\operatorname{AllFail}\).

symbols.name: MAG
symbols.role: Graph component of a failure certificate.

symbols.name: sADMG
symbols.type: represented selected acyclic directed mixed graph
symbols.role: Selected graphical realization of the certificate.

symbols.name: F
symbols.role: Larger forest in the selected hedge.

symbols.name: Fprime
symbols.def: \(F'\subsetneq F\).
symbols.role: Smaller forest in the selected hedge.

symbols.name: Rroot
symbols.def: \(R_F\) denotes the common root set of \(F\) and \(F'\).
symbols.role: Common root set of the nested forests in a generic certificate.

symbols.name: Obow
symbols.def: \(O_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b,Y_b,C_b\}\).
symbols.role: Observed vertices of the explicit selected-bow realization.

symbols.name: Lbow
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{U_b\}\).
symbols.role: Latent vertices of the explicit selected-bow realization.

symbols.name: Dbow
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{bow}}\) has vertex partition \(O_{\mathrm{bow}}\dot\cup L_{\mathrm{bow}}\dot\cup\{S_b\}\) and edge set \(\{U_b\to X_b,U_b\to Y_b,X_b\to Y_b,Y_b\to S_b\}\), with \(C_b\) isolated.
symbols.role: Underlying causal graph of both explicit rational mechanisms.

symbols.name: Gbow
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{bow}}\) has observed and selection structure \(X_b\to Y_b\), \(X_b\leftrightarrow Y_b\), and \(Y_b\to S_b\), with \(C_b\) isolated.
symbols.role: Latent projection of the selected-bow DAG retaining the selection node.

symbols.name: Mbow
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bow}}\) is the MAG on \(\{X_b,Y_b,C_b\}\) with the undirected edge \(X_b-Y_b\) and isolated \(C_b\).
symbols.role: MAG induced because both \(X_b\) and \(Y_b\) are ancestors of selection.

symbols.name: Pbow
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bow}}\) has the edge \(X_b\mathbin{\circ\! -\! \circ}Y_b\) and isolated \(C_b\).
symbols.role: Equivalence-class graph represented by the selected-bow MAG.

symbols.name: Abow
symbols.def: \(A_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{Y_b,C_b\}\).
symbols.role: Terminal joint target of the root sIDP call.

symbols.name: Bbow
symbols.def: \(B_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b\}\).
symbols.role: Terminal intervention of the root sIDP call.

symbols.name: traceBow
symbols.def: \(\pi_{\mathrm{bow}}=\varepsilon\) is the empty role trace at \(\rho=(\{X_b\},\{C_b\})\).
symbols.role: Reachability witness for the root role state.

symbols.name: Fbow
symbols.def: \(F_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{X_b,Y_b\},\{X_b\to Y_b,X_b\leftrightarrow Y_b\})\).
symbols.role: Larger forest in the explicit selected hedge.

symbols.name: Fbowprime
symbols.def: \(F'_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{Y_b\},\varnothing)\).
symbols.role: Proper subforest in the explicit selected hedge.

symbols.name: Rbow
symbols.def: \(R_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{Y_b\}\).
symbols.role: Common root set of the explicit nested forests.

symbols.name: Dmax
symbols.def: \(D_{\max,\mathrm{bow}}=\varnothing\).
symbols.role: Maximal selection-exchange set in the Chen--Mooij selected-hedge criterion.

symbols.name: M0
symbols.role: First witness model.

symbols.name: M1
symbols.role: Second witness model.

symbols.name: Mpos
symbols.role: Selected-bow mechanism \(\mathbf M_+\) indexed by \(\sigma=+1\).

symbols.name: Mneg
symbols.role: Selected-bow mechanism \(\mathbf M_-\) indexed by \(\sigma=-1\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma=(\rho,\mathcal M,\mathcal G,F,F',\mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1)\) together with a role trace and expanded rational evaluation tables.
symbols.role: Checkable nonidentification output.

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: \(\theta\) is a strictly positive rational local conditional-probability table whose entries sum to one within every conditioning block.
symbols.role: Baseline varying mechanism for an affine witness family.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T=\{w\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(\theta)}:\sum_{j\text{ in each conditional-probability block}}w_j=0\}\).
symbols.role: Admissible normalized perturbation directions.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: The columns of \(R\) form a rational basis of \(T\).
symbols.role: Coordinates normalized local-mechanism perturbations.

symbols.name: q
symbols.role: Coordinate vector for an admissible perturbation.

symbols.name: v
symbols.role: Normalized direction varying one local mechanism.

symbols.name: t
symbols.role: Scale in \(\theta(t)=\theta+t v\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.role: Selected-law and denominator-lock constraints.

symbols.name: b
symbols.role: Terminal numerator contrast.

symbols.name: AT
symbols.role: Selected-law and denominator-lock constraints in simplex-tangent coordinates.

symbols.name: bT
symbols.role: Terminal numerator contrast in simplex-tangent coordinates.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.role: Radius preserving strict positivity of the perturbed rational mechanism.

symbols.name: BOW
symbols.role: Positive rational regression test for denominator locking.

symbols.name: Hextract
symbols.role: Concrete starting move for the open converse construction.

symbols.name: formulaDAG
symbols.role: Cache of region decompositions, fixing attempts, and repeated subexpressions.

symbols.name: Lcert
symbols.def: \(L_{\Gamma}\) is the total bit length of the graph data, dense full-assignment probability expansion, mechanism tables, and arithmetic evaluation trace in \(\Gamma\).
symbols.role: Output and verification size.

symbols.name: Lout
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{out}}\) is the bit length of the returned shared formula DAG or the expanded certificate \(\Gamma\).
symbols.role: Output-sensitive synthesis size.

symbols.name: Qobs
symbols.def: When \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is rational, \(Q_{\mathrm{obs}}=(Q_{\mathrm{obs}}(z):z\in\{0,1\}^V)\) is its normalized full-table encoding by binary numerators and denominators.
symbols.role: Optional numerical input used only after symbolic formula synthesis.

symbols.name: Lin
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{in}}\) is the total bit length of the encoded table \(Q_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
symbols.role: Bit-size parameter for formula evaluation.

symbols.name: Leval
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{eval}}\) is the bit length of the exact rational numerical evaluation output.
symbols.role: Output-size parameter for exact numerical evaluation.

symbols.name: FC
symbols.role: Shared-cache implementation of Branch-sCIDP and witness synthesis.

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.role: Checks graphical membership, forest conditions, rational SCM factorization, and the denominator lock.

symbols.name: Eval
symbols.role: Separately evaluates a synthesized symbolic formula against an encoded rational probability table.

symbols.name: PAGId
symbols.def: The public implementation of the no-selection IDP and CIDP algorithms.
symbols.role: Concrete downstream consumer.

standard.name: Disjoint intervention, outcome, and conditioning sets
Positive discrete selected SCM represented by a COPAG

novel.justification: Binary treatments, outcomes, and recorded eligibility indicators are common in selected-cohort studies, and full-support binary laws allow latent confounding and nonconstant ascertainment while forming the first nontrivial class in which an explicit denominator-locked certificate can be demanded.

definitions.name: Positive binary observed selected-SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M:\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P),\ \operatorname{range}_{\mathbf M}(V)=\{0,1\}^V\}\)

definitions.name: Identification from the selected observational law
definitions.construction: \(\psi\ \text{is identified over }\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1}\Rightarrow\psi_{\mathbf M_0}(y;x,c)=\psi_{\mathbf M_1}(y;x,c)\bigr]\ \text{for all }\mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\)

definitions.name: Treatment--condition role state
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R(W)=\{(\bar X,\bar C):\bar X\subseteq W,\ \bar C=W\setminus\bar X\}\)

definitions.name: Legal bucket-intersection Rule-2 exchange
definitions.construction: For \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) and \(B_i\in\mathfrak B(\mathcal P)\), a treatment-to-condition edge moves the nonempty block \(T=B_i\cap\bar X\) to \((\bar X\setminus T,\bar C\cup T)\) when \(Y\perp I_T\mid\bar X\cup\bar C\) in \(\mathcal P_{\operatorname{do}(I_T,\bar X\setminus T)}\); a condition-to-treatment edge moves the nonempty block \(T=B_i\cap\bar C\) to \((\bar X\cup T,\bar C\setminus T)\) when \(Y\perp I_T\mid\bar X\cup\bar C\) in \(\mathcal P_{\operatorname{do}(I_T,\bar X)}\). Assignments travel with their variables.

definitions.name: Reachable role-state graph
definitions.construction: \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) is the directed graph obtained by breadth-first search from \((X,C)\) using every edge satisfying \(\text{def:legal-role-exchange}\), storing one nonrepeating trace to each reached state.

definitions.name: Terminal joint, denominator, and numerator
definitions.construction: At \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), set \(J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y,\bar C=\bar c\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1)\), \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)=\sum_{y'}J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\), and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)\).

definitions.name: Branch-sCIDP
definitions.construction: Enumerate every \(\rho\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\). At each state run \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;Y\cup\bar C,\bar X,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) treated as a formal probability-table indeterminate. On the first success with joint functional \(F_\rho(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), return the symbolic normalized formula \(F_\rho(y,\bar c;\bar x)/\sum_{y'}F_\rho(y',\bar c;\bar x)\) transported back along the stored trace. Return \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) only if every reachable call fails.

definitions.name: Denominator-locked selected conditional hedge certificate
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma\) consists of a reachable terminal state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) and trace, \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\), a represented selected graph \(\mathcal G\in[\mathcal M]_{\mathsf G}\), and nested \(R_F\)-rooted C-forests \(F'\subsetneq F\). The forest predicates require \(V(F)\cap\bar X\neq\varnothing\), \(V(F')\cap\bar X=\varnothing\), \(R_F\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\operatorname{do}(\bar X)}}(Y\cup\bar C\cup\{S\})\), and the Chen--Mooij selected-hedge conditions for \((Y\cup\bar C\cup\{S\},\bar X)\) at the maximal valid selection-exchange set. They do not require every vertex of \(Y\cup\bar C\) to occur in the forests. The certificate also contains positive rational binary SCMs \(\mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\) such that \(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1}\), \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(\bar c;\bar x)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(\bar c;\bar x)>0\), and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(y,\bar c;\bar x)\neq N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(y,\bar c;\bar x)\).

definitions.name: Affine denominator-lock rank system
definitions.construction: Fix a finite binary latent realization of a selected graph represented by \(\mathcal P\), a strictly positive rational baseline local mechanism \(\theta\), and strictly positive rational tables for every other fixed mechanism, with every conditional-probability block normalized. Let \(T=\{w\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(\theta)}:\sum_{j\text{ in each conditional-probability block}}w_j=0\}\), and choose any rational basis matrix \(R\) for \(T\). For an arbitrary ambient rational direction \(w\), set \(\theta_w(t)=\theta+t w\), \(o_{z,w}(t)=P_{\theta_w(t)}(V=z,S=\mathbf 1)\), \(Z_{o,w}(t)=\sum_z o_{z,w}(t)\), \(h_w(t)=P_{\theta_w(t)}(\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\), \(k_w(t)=P_{\theta_w(t)}(Y=y,\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\), and \(Z_{x,w}(t)=P_{\theta_w(t)}(S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\). Define the rational matrix \(A\) so that \(Aw\) is the vector of coefficients of \(t\) in \(Z_{o,w}(0)o_{z,w}(t)-o_{z,w}(0)Z_{o,w}(t)\) for all \(z\), followed by the coefficient of \(t\) in \(Z_{x,w}(0)h_w(t)-h_w(0)Z_{x,w}(t)\). Define the rational row \(b\) so that \(bw\) is the coefficient of \(t\) in \(Z_{x,w}(0)k_w(t)-k_w(0)Z_{x,w}(t)\). For \(q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\), put \(v=Rq\), \(\theta(t)=\theta+t v\), \(A_T=AR\), and \(b_T=bR\).

definitions.name: Selected-bow DAG, sADMG, MAG, and COPAG
definitions.construction: Take distinct binary vertices \(U_b,X_b,Y_b,C_b,S_b\) and the singleton specialization \(X=\{X_b\}\), \(Y=\{Y_b\}\), \(C=\{C_b\}\), and \(S=\{S_b\}\). Set \(O_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b,Y_b,C_b\}\), \(L_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{U_b\}\), and let \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{bow}}\) be the DAG on \(O_{\mathrm{bow}}\dot\cup L_{\mathrm{bow}}\dot\cup\{S_b\}\) with edges \(U_b\to X_b\), \(U_b\to Y_b\), \(X_b\to Y_b\), and \(Y_b\to S_b\), with \(C_b\) isolated. Its selected latent projection is \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{X_b,Y_b,C_b,S_b\},\{X_b\to Y_b,X_b\leftrightarrow Y_b,Y_b\to S_b\})\), with \(C_b\) isolated. Because \(X_b\) and \(Y_b\) are ancestors of \(S_b\), set \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{X_b,Y_b,C_b\},\{X_b-Y_b\})\), with \(C_b\) isolated. Set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bow}}\) to the input-free COPAG with \(X_b\mathbin{\circ\! -\! \circ}Y_b\) and isolated \(C_b\).

definitions.name: Positive rational selected-bow template
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{bow}}\), let \(U_b\) and \(C_b\) be independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) variables, let \(P(X_b=1\mid U_b=0)=1/4\) and \(P(X_b=1\mid U_b=1)=3/4\), and define \(r_a=P(U_b=1\mid X_b=a)\), so \(r_0=1/4\) and \(r_1=3/4\). For \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), set \(P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a,U_b=d)=1/2+\sigma(d-r_a)/4\), \(P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=0)=1/3\), and \(P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=1)=2/3\), for \(a,d\in\{0,1\}\). Denote the \(\sigma=+1\) and \(\sigma=-1\) models by \(\mathbf M_+\) and \(\mathbf M_-\), respectively. Fix \(\rho=(\{X_b\},\{C_b\})\) and the assignments \(x(X_b)=0\), \(c(C_b)=1\), and \(y(Y_b)=1\).

definitions.name: Selected-bow terminal-joint hedge objects
definitions.construction: At the root role state \(\rho=(\{X_b\},\{C_b\})\), take the empty trace \(\pi_{\mathrm{bow}}=\varepsilon\), the terminal joint target \(A_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{Y_b,C_b\}\), and the intervention set \(B_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b\}\). Set \(F_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{X_b,Y_b\},\{X_b\to Y_b,X_b\leftrightarrow Y_b\})\), \(F'_{\mathrm{bow}}=(\{Y_b\},\varnothing)\), \(R_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{Y_b\}\), and the maximal selection-exchange set \(D_{\max,\mathrm{bow}}=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Residual-forest extraction handle
definitions.construction: Starting from an all-branches-fail role graph, choose a reachable terminal state maximal in its intervention role and then minimal in its remaining anterior region. Adapt the Chen--Mooij residual tuple and represented-MAG orientation to the entire terminal treatment set. Trace root-to-outcome and root-to-selection paths in the resulting forest. Use failed alternative exchanges to eliminate pure conditioning-factor directions, and use the affine rank system, or a multi-mechanism rational extension of it, to synthesize the denominator-locked model pair.

definitions.name: Shared-cache formula-or-certificate solver
definitions.construction: Given only \(\mathcal P,Y,X,C\), \(\operatorname{FC}\) runs Branch-sCIDP while caching, for each subset of \(V\), its deterministic region decomposition, leaf fixing attempts, identified symbolic kernels, and formula-DAG nodes. On \(\operatorname{AllFail}\), it invokes \(H_{\mathrm{extract}}\) and streams the expanded rational certificate. \(\operatorname{Verify}\) checks the role trace, represented-graph and forest conditions, local mechanism factorization, dense full-assignment sums, equality of the two induced selected laws, denominator equality and positivity, and numerator inequality. Numerical evaluation is a separate call \(\operatorname{Eval}(\mathsf{DAG},Q_{\mathrm{obs}})\) on an encoded rational probability table.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\), every \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\), and every binary assignment \((\bar x,\bar c)\), \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)>0\).
statements.justification: Normalization must be a legitimate pointwise operation throughout the reachable role graph.
statements.gap: Chen--Mooij obtain pointwise conditional kernels under positivity; the present lemma records the exact denominator needed by every branch.
statements.consumer: The Branch-sCIDP formula evaluator can reject no positive-model input because of a zero terminal denominator.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) returns a normalized symbolic functional at a reachable state \(\rho\), its evaluation at \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) equals \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\) inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). If \(\Gamma\) verifies, then \(\psi\) is not identified over \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\). Moreover, \(|\Omega|\leq 2^{|W|}\), and every stored nonrepeating trace has length at most \(2^{|W|}-1\).
statements.justification: This theorem separates the settled soundness direction from the genuinely open converse.
statements.gap: Chen--Mooij prove soundness for their scheduled sCIDP; this result covers exhaustive legal role-state branching and checkable locked certificates.
statements.consumer: PAGId can safely report every returned selected-cohort formula and every verified failure certificate.

statements.statement: For the rational interior one-mechanism family in \(\text{def:affine-rank-system}\), there exists \(q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\) satisfying \(A_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}([A_T;b_T])>\operatorname{rank}(A_T)\). Equivalently, \(v=Rq\in T\cap\mathbb Q^{\dim(\theta)}\) preserves the complete normalized selected observational law and \(D_{\rho}\) exactly while changing \(N_{\rho}\). This criterion is independent of the chosen rational basis \(R\). For every such \(q\), interior positivity gives a rational \(\delta>0\) such that every rational \(t\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) leaves \(\theta+t v\) positive and normalized; the baseline and perturbed mechanisms therefore define positive rational binary SCMs \(\mathbf M_0\) and \(\mathbf M_1\) with equal \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and equal positive \(D_{\rho}\), but unequal \(N_{\rho}\).
statements.justification: The rank inequality turns denominator locking from an informal perturbation idea into exact rational linear algebra.
statements.gap: Classical hedge constructions separate an interventional distribution but do not impose equality of a selected conditional denominator.
statements.consumer: The residual-forest extractor can certify candidate local templates by tangent-restricted rational row reduction.

statements.statement: The graph \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bow}}\) belongs to \([\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bow}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{bow}}\) belongs to \([\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bow}}]_{\mathsf G}\). The sign-indexed models \(\mathbf M_+\) and \(\mathbf M_-\) induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{bow}}\) and lie in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{bow}})\). For either sign and each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(P_{\sigma}(U_b=1\mid X_b=a)=r_a\), hence \(P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a)=1/2\). Therefore, for each \(a,d\in\{0,1\}\), \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=1,S_b=1)=1/12\), \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=0,S_b=1)=1/24\), and \(P_{\sigma}(S_b=1)=1/2\), proving \(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_+}=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_-}\). Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_b=0)\), \(P_{\mathbf M_+}(Y_b=1)=9/16\) and \(P_{\mathbf M_-}(Y_b=1)=7/16\), while \(P_{\mathbf M_+}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))=25/48\) and \(P_{\mathbf M_-}(S_b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_b=0))=23/48\). At \(\rho=(\{X_b\},\{C_b\})\) with \(x(X_b)=0\), \(c(C_b)=1\), and \(y(Y_b)=1\), it follows that \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_+}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_-}(1;0)=1/2\), \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_+}(1,1;0)=9/25\), and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_-}(1,1;0)=7/23\), giving \(\psi_{\mathbf M_+}(y;x,c)=18/25\) and \(\psi_{\mathbf M_-}(y;x,c)=14/23\). The empty trace reaches the root terminal target \(A_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{Y_b,C_b\}\) under \(B_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b\}\). The forests \(F_{\mathrm{bow}}\) and \(F'_{\mathrm{bow}}\) are nested \(R_{\mathrm{bow}}\)-rooted C-forests, \(F'_{\mathrm{bow}}\subsetneq F_{\mathrm{bow}}\), \(V(F_{\mathrm{bow}})\cap B_{\mathrm{bow}}=\{X_b\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{bow}})\cap B_{\mathrm{bow}}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{bow}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{bow}},\operatorname{do}(X_b)}(\{Y_b,C_b\}\cup\{S_b\})\). The maximal selection-exchange set is \(D_{\max,\mathrm{bow}}=\varnothing\), and \((F_{\mathrm{bow}},F'_{\mathrm{bow}})\) is a Chen--Mooij selected hedge for \((\{Y_b,C_b,S_b\},\{X_b\})\). The isolated terminal outcome vertex \(C_b\) need not be a forest vertex because the hedge criterion uses the common-root and postintervention ancestor predicates.
statements.justification: A nondegenerate exact witness ties denominator locking to an explicit DAG, its selected projection, a represented MAG and COPAG, and a valid target-level selected hedge.
statements.gap: The source completeness proof supplies unconditional selected obstructions but no explicit positive rational locked conditional witness.
statements.consumer: The witness is a mandatory regression case for the bounded enumeration and certificate verifier.

statements.statement: Whenever every state \(\rho\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) fails its terminal sIDP call, does the handle \(H_{\mathrm{extract}}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C,\Omega)\) construct a denominator-locked certificate \(\Gamma\) with positive rational binary mechanisms for the entire terminal intervention, and can this construction be streamed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations? Equivalently, can every graph-forced cancellation that defeats a proposed lock be converted into a legal role-state exchange reaching a nonfailing terminal joint?
statements.justification: This is the sole load-bearing converse step: ordinary joint nonidentifiability does not by itself prevent normalization from canceling it.
statements.gap: Neither Chen--Mooij's represented selected forest nor the no-selection conditional hedge arguments coordinate all reachable terminal states while preserving a selected denominator.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields a complete graphical failure certificate; a smallest counterexample from the bounded search would decisively pivot the algorithmic characterization.

statements.statement: For every query satisfying the maintained conditions and over the full-support binary observed subclass \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\), \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) returns a normalized symbolic formula if and only if \(\psi\) is identified. If Branch-sCIDP returns \(\operatorname{AllFail}\), \(\operatorname{FC}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) returns a denominator-locked certificate \(\Gamma\). On this binary subclass, the result strictly tightens Chen--Mooij's soundness-only conditional conclusion to an if-and-only-if formula-or-certificate characterization. It makes no completeness claim for nonbinary observed alphabets and reduces to the no-selection CIDP boundary when \(S=\varnothing\).
statements.justification: An exact identification boundary on the first nontrivial full-support binary subclass isolates the normalization obstruction in selected conditional PAG analysis.
statements.gap: Chen--Mooij explicitly leave sCIDP completeness open even on the binary slice of their positive discrete class. Abouei and coauthors give only a sufficient condition and sound algorithm for the unconditional selected target \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) in one known augmented ADMG and conjecture completeness; they do not address conditioning on \(C=c\), COPAG uncertainty, exhaustive legal role exchanges, or denominator-locked rational countermodels.
statements.consumer: Selected-cohort FCI analyses obtain a definitive answer rather than a sound formula or an uninterpreted failure flag.

statements.statement: Given the encoded graph and query \((\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\), the shared-cache algorithm \(\operatorname{FC}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) returns the symbolic formula or expanded rational certificate of \(\text{thm:complete-characterization}\) in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{out}})\) bit operations, where repeated identified kernels are represented once in the formula DAG. The verifier \(\operatorname{Verify}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C,\Gamma)\) accepts exactly valid expanded certificates in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations. Separately, when the rational selected law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is supplied as the encoded table \(Q_{\mathrm{obs}}\) of length \(L_{\mathrm{in}}\), \(\operatorname{Eval}\) evaluates a returned formula DAG exactly in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{out}}+L_{\mathrm{in}}+L_{\mathrm{eval}})\) bit operations.
statements.justification: Completeness is operational only if formulas share repeated work and failures are checkable in their explicit encoding.
statements.gap: Existing PAG identification algorithms return formulas or failure flags; they do not synthesize and verify expanded positive rational selected countermodels.
statements.consumer: PAGId can expose a reproducible failure object whose verification cost is polynomial in what the user receives.

statements.statement: When \(S=\varnothing\), Branch-sCIDP and CIDP agree on the identification decision for \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\); every successful Branch-sCIDP output is algebraically equivalent to a CIDP identifying functional, and every all-fail certificate reduces to a valid no-selection conditional nonidentifiability witness.
statements.justification: The standard no-selection case is the required regression against the established complete conditional-PAG theory.
statements.gap: The result is not a novelty claim; it prevents the selected extension from changing the settled no-selection identification boundary.
statements.consumer: PAGId retains its current CIDP behavior when selection is absent.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from the exact selected observational law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}=P(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\); symbolic formula synthesis takes only the graph and query, and no sampling asymptotics are imposed.
sampling_model.units: A finite system of binary observed variables indexed by \(V\), with arbitrary finite latent and selection variables in the represented selected SCM.
sampling_model.treatment: Hard interventions \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), with legal Rule-2 exchanges of current bucket intersections.
sampling_model.overlap: The maintained full-support binary subclass of the Chen--Mooij positive discrete model class makes every evaluated selected conditioning denominator strictly positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; numerical evaluation is a separate exact-arithmetic operation on an explicitly encoded rational selected probability table.

estimand_functional: \(\psi(y;x,c)=F_{\rho}(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\big/\sum_{y'}F_{\rho}(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\quad\text{for a successful }\rho\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Soundness follows directly, while we leave completeness to future work.
For one known augmented ADMG with latent variables, a sufficient graphical condition and a sound algorithm identify \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) from \(P(V\mid S=1)\), while completeness is conjectured.
Alg. 2 is complete for identifying conditional effects.
Conditional interventional distributions admit a complete identification algorithm for a specified semi-Markovian graph.
The algorithm is complete for unconditional causal-effect identification from a PAG.
The classical hedge criterion is incorrect as stated, although a hedge arises at ID failure.
Even sound and complete identification solutions do not solve verification of a supplied formula.

tldr: For the full-support binary observed subclass of finite input-free selected COPAG models, the project characterizes identification of \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid \operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)\) by an exhaustive role-state version of sCIDP. A successful branch supplies a symbolic normalized observed-law functional. If every branch fails, the proposed converse constructs a represented selected graph, a terminal-joint forest obstruction, and two positive rational binary structural causal models that agree on the full selected observational law and on the positive conditioning denominator but disagree on the joint numerator. The denominator lock rules out cancellation after normalization. The explicit selected-bow regression case fixes the underlying DAG, selected projection, represented MAG and COPAG, root-state forests, empty maximal selection-exchange set, and rational calculations. A graph-and-query algorithm returns either a shared symbolic formula DAG or an expanded rational certificate with output-sensitive exponential synthesis and polynomial certificate verification; evaluation against an encoded rational probability table is analyzed separately.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij prove completeness of sIDP for unconditional selected interventional kernels and soundness of sCIDP, but explicitly leave conditional completeness and the appropriate conditional hedge criterion open. This proposal addresses that open issue only on their full-support binary observed subclass. Abouei and coauthors study \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) from \(P(V\mid S=1)\) with latent variables in one known augmented ADMG, provide a sufficient condition and sound algorithm, and conjecture completeness; they do not treat an equivalence class or postintervention conditioning on \(C=c\). Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim prove conditional completeness for PAGs without selection, where a converse need not preserve a selected conditioning denominator.
project_justification.niche: Conditional normalization can eliminate nonidentifiability of a joint intervention. On the first nontrivial binary certificate class under latent selection, a valid failure witness must preserve both the entire selected observational law and the terminal conditioning denominator while changing the terminal joint numerator.
project_justification.fill: Branch-sCIDP exhausts legal Rule-2 role exchanges before invoking sIDP on the binary subclass. Its converse is reduced to a denominator-locked residual-forest extraction question, supported by an exact simplex-tangent rank criterion for positive rational mechanism perturbations and a fully specified positive rational selected-bow witness. That witness verifies the DAG, selected projection, represented MAG and COPAG, and the named nested root forests; the isolated vertex \(C_b\) is licensed by the standard root and postintervention ancestor predicates rather than being inserted artificially into a forest. From the graph and query alone, the final procedure returns either a symbolic normalized formula or an independently checkable expanded rational certificate; evaluation of the formula uses a separately encoded rational probability table.

related_work: Chen and Mooij's Theorems 4.14 and 4.15 establish soundness and completeness of sIDP for unconditional selected kernels on input-free COPAGs; their concluding sCIDP section proves soundness and explicitly leaves completeness and a conditional hedge analogue open. The present completeness claim tightens that soundness-only result on the deliberately restricted full-support binary observed subclass, not on their whole arbitrary finite positive-discrete class; extension to nonbinary observed alphabets remains open. Their selected-hedge predicates are used at the complete terminal intervention target and require common roots in the relevant postintervention ancestor set, not inclusion of every isolated terminal outcome vertex in a forest. Abouei, Mokhtarian, Kiyavash, and Grossglauser study S-ID from \(P(V\mid S=1)\) to \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) with latent variables in one known augmented ADMG, introduce selected counterparts of c-components and hedges, give a sufficient graphical condition and a sound algorithm, and conjecture rather than prove completeness. Their result informs the selected-hedge comparison but neither handles PAG or COPAG uncertainty nor proves completeness. The present binary problem instead ranges over a COPAG equivalence class, additionally conditions on \(C=c\) after intervention, exhausts legal role exchanges, seeks an if-and-only-if characterization, and returns a denominator-locked positive rational countermodel certificate on failure. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim's Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4 establish complete conditional identification from PAGs without selection and inform the role-exchange architecture; the selected binary result is not presented as a strict strengthening of their theorem. Shpitser and Pearl give the fixed-graph conditional identification benchmark. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim supply the unconditional PAG represented-graph construction. Shpitser's 2023 correction shows why a hedge must be tied to the complete intervention target rather than an arbitrary subset. Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij supply the SCM semantics of conditioning on latent selection. Forré and Mooij supply the input-kernel calculus but make no completeness claim for that extension. Bellot and Duarte and coauthors motivate distinct sharp-bounds and discrete-certificate alternatives; neither gives binary selected-PAG conditional point-identification completeness. Hwang and coauthors propagate formula-specific positivity through graphical identification, but leave complete positivity-aware conditional algorithms open. Freni, Henckel, and Weichwald study verification of a supplied interventional formula, a complementary task that does not synthesize denominator-locked nonidentification certificates.
technical_internal_limitation: A varying conditional effect need not admit two models with the same denominator: the abstract fiber \((D,N)=(d,d^2)\) has no horizontal pair. In a selected-bow variant, making \(C_b\) an informative child of \(Y_b\) can also make a one-mechanism perturbation fail the lock. Therefore ordinary semantic nonidentifiability, a single selected hedge, or failure of one affine template does not prove the requested converse. The proof must derive graph-compatible freedom from simultaneous branch failure or find a counterexample.
honest_scope: The soundness theorem, finite role-state bound, simplex-tangent affine rank criterion, and calculated selected-bow witness are tractable supporting claims, all with status \(\text{to-prove}\). The bow proposition includes the graph-representation and selected-hedge checks for its named DAG, sADMG, MAG, COPAG, forests, roots, and empty selection-exchange set; it does not substitute for extracting such objects from an arbitrary all-fail role graph. The complete residual-forest-to-rational-model construction and its output-sensitive bit complexity are open and are isolated in \(\text{oeq:denominator-locked-extraction}\). The headline theorem depends on that open node. The identification domain has full binary observed support; no finite-alphabet lift is claimed, and nonbinary observed alphabets remain open. The claim is not fiberwise, faithful, generic, continuous-variable, or input-aware. When selection is absent, the proposal collapses to the established CIDP boundary. The early kill test enumerates input-free COPAGs with at most four observed vertices and exact role-state graphs; an all-branches-fail identified query or a failing nonidentified query that forbids every locked rational pair rejects the kernel.
